caption_or_description: A microscopic view of magnetic domains in a crystal of iron. The blue arrows pointing in different directions tell us that these domains are not aligned.

Pieces of iron in successive stages of magnetization. The arrows represent domains; the head is a north pole and the tail is a south pole. Poles of neighboring domains neutralize each other's effects, except at the two ends of a piece of iron.
Wai Tsan Lee shows iron nails that have become induced magnets.
